:::{#exm-canonical-links}
#### Canonical links of three families

We apply @thm-canonical-link-inverse,
using $b'(\theta)$ from @exm-edf-mean-variance.

- **Gaussian**: $b'(\theta) = \theta$, so $\invf{b'}(\mu) = \mu$,
  and the canonical link is the identity link $g(\mu) = \mu$.

- **Poisson**: $\mu = b'(\theta) = e^\theta$,
  so $\theta = \logf{\mu}$,
  and the canonical link is the log link $g(\mu) = \logf{\mu}$.
  At $\mu = 3$, $g(3) = \logf{3} \approx 1.0986$.

For the **Bernoulli** distribution, we solve $\mu = b'(\theta) = \expit(\theta)$ for $\theta$:

$$
\ba
\mu &= \frac{e^\theta}{1 + e^\theta}
&& \text{(definition of } \expit\text{)}
\\ \mu (1 + e^\theta) &= e^\theta
&& \text{(multiply both sides by } 1 + e^\theta\text{)}
\\ \mu + \mu e^\theta &= e^\theta
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\ \mu &= e^\theta - \mu e^\theta
&& \text{(subtract } \mu e^\theta \text{ from both sides)}
\\ &= e^\theta (1 - \mu)
&& \text{(factor out } e^\theta\text{)}
\\ \frac{\mu}{1 - \mu} &= e^\theta
&& \text{(divide by } 1 - \mu\text{)}
\\ \logit(\mu) &= \theta
&& \text{(take logs)}
\ea
$$

So the canonical link is the logit link.
At $\mu = 0.25$,
$g(0.25) = \logf{0.25 / 0.75} = \logf{1/3} \approx -1.0986$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-noncanonical-link}
#### A link that is not canonical

The probit link $g(\mu) = \Phi^{-1}(\mu)$,
where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function,
is a valid link function for a Bernoulli outcome,
because it is strictly increasing on $(0, 1)$.
It is not the canonical link:
at $\mu = 0.25$,
$\Phi^{-1}(0.25) \approx -0.6745$,
whereas the natural parameter is
$\theta = \logit(0.25) \approx -1.0986$
(@exm-canonical-links).
:::
